<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided `tunarr.install` script contains two functions: `post_install` and `post_upgrade`. The `post_install` function checks if a VERSION file exists in `/var/lib/tunarr/data.ms/`. If it does, it reads the stored database version and compares it with the version of the installed `tunarr-meilisearch` binary using `sort -V` to determine if a version mismatch (specifically, a downgrade) has occurred. If the current database version is greater than the new Meilisearch version, a warning message is printed advising the user to manually remove files from `/var/lib/tunarr/data.ms/*` and rescan libraries.

All operations are confined to version checking and user notification. The script reads only from predefined, application-specific paths and writes no data. It executes no network operations, spawns no external processes beyond `tunarr-meilisearch --version` and standard shell utilities (which are expected in this context), and performs no file modifications. The `post_upgrade` function simply delegates to `post_install`, which is a common and safe pattern in AUR install scripts. There is no obfuscated code, unexpected system modifications, or data exfiltration.

The script behaves as a typical post-install helper for a local application managing compatibility between persistent data and executable versions. All actions are transparent, limited in scope, and aligned with the expected behavior of a package managing version compatibility during upgrades.
</details>
